title: Rabbi Levi bar Chama
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Berakhot 5a: “Rabbi Levi bar Chama said that Resh Lakish said: A person should always incite his good inclination against his evil inclination,” etc. He likewise said there in his name: “What is the meaning of what is written, ‘And I will give you the tablets’? — this teaches that all of them were given to Moses at Sinai.” Dikdukei Soferim reads Rabbi Levi bar Lachma. In Sukkah 47a: “Rabbi Yochanan said: One says the time-blessing on Shemini … and Rabbi Levi bar Chama — and some say Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina — said: Know,” etc. There too Dikdukei Soferim reads bar Lachma, and so it is in the Pesaro, Venice and Constantinople printings.

In Taanit 16a: “Why do they put ashes on the head of each and every one? Rabbi Levi bar Chama and Rabbi Chanina disagree on it … and why do they go out to the cemetery? Rabbi Levi bar Chama and Rabbi Chanina disagree on it.” Dikdukei Soferim reads Rabbi Levi bar Lachma and Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina.

In Zevachim 53b: “Rabbi Levi bar Chama said that Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said: A strip went out,” etc.; Dikdukei Soferim reads Rabbi Levi bar Lachma. And indeed we find in Rosh Hashanah 29b: “Rabbi Levi bar Lachma said that Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said”; and in Bava Batra 15a: “Rabbi Levi bar Lachma said: Job lived in the days of Moses.” Hyman regards these as undoubtedly the names of one Amora.

notes.text: Initial ר״ל is Resh Lakish; the later ר״ל בר לחמא means Rabbi Levi bar Lachma by connection with the full name in the same entry. Chama/Lachma and Chanina/Chama son of Chanina variants remain visible. Hyman’s undoubtedly-one-person conclusion retains its force and attribution.

The consulted Berakhot 5a text directly names Levi bar Chama reporting Shimon ben Lakish in both sayings. The Lachma, Dikdukei Soferim and named early-print readings are reported by Hyman here; those exact editions were not independently inspected. His undoubtedly-one-Amora conclusion remains his own.
